content:
The image shows a banana plant with:
- Older leaves collapsed and dried, hanging down around the pseudostem like a skirt
- Significant leaf collapse and browning of the older/outer leaves
- Young green suckers emerging at the base while the main plant is dying
- Visible damage/splitting at the base of the pseudostem
- Wilting progression from older to younger leaves

This pattern is the hallmark of **Panama Disease** (Fusarium wilt): leaves collapse at the petiole and hang down the pseudostem, older leaves die first, and the pseudostem base shows splitting. The presence of healthy young suckers while the parent plant collapses is also characteristic. There are no leaf streaks/spots (ruling out Sigatoka), no bunching at the top (ruling out Bunchy Top), and no fruit symptoms visible.
